_about: 灯谜 for 周衡's replays (Hanli 2026-11-02: the story's 人参 riddle won four times). Every riddle here is old and public domain, copied from the source it names (`source`, a key of `sources`; `at` where in it) with the answer that source itself gives — none written for this game. Chinese texts are simplified from the sources' traditional characters; the ——打一物 tail is the board's, as the 红楼梦's own riddles carry one; a riddle whose wordplay works only in traditional glyphs (習 · 圖 · 畢 · 資 · 蘭, the 车中猴 申) is left out. English lines keep the source's spelling, its verse lines joined by ' / '. `answers` are the source's answer and the plain ways a player names it (the page judges, jinchat-games.js checkRiddle); `hints` (two, graded) and `choices` (four, one right) are this game's, not the source's. The story deals it by `deal.pool: 'dengmi'` (tasks/world.json zhishi-shen): the first play — n 0, a fresh save and an errand's first play alike — asks the chat's own 人参 riddle; each win after it (Look's `n`, rules/pool.mjs poolDeal) draws the next of this pool in the board's language, in an order its save's `seed` decides, every one asked once before any comes round again (jinchat-games.js poolPick). The 游戏厅's row walks the same pool in this browser.

zh.q: 猴子身轻站树梢。——打一果名。
hints: 猴子站上枝头——「立枝」，念快些。
岭南的果子，红壳白肉。

zh.q: 身自端方，体自坚硬。虽不能言，有言必应。——打一用物。
hints: 书案上的，写字离不了它。
磨墨用的那块方石头——「有言（研）必应」。

zh.q: 能使妖魔胆尽摧，身如束帛气如雷。一声震得人方恐，回首相看已化灰。——打一物。
hints: 过年才放，一点就响。
竹筒里装着火药，响一声就成了灰。

zh.q: 天运人功理不穷，有功无运也难逢。因何镇日纷纷乱，只为阴阳数不同。——打一物。
hints: 执事堂里，周衡天天拨它。
上珠是阳，下珠是阴，拨来拨去为的是一个数。

zh.q: 阶下儿童仰面时，清明妆点最堪宜。游丝一断浑无力，莫向东风怨别离。——打一物。
hints: 孩子仰着脸看它，清明前后最多。
一根线牵着它，线一断就飘走了。

zh.q: 前身色相总无成，不听菱歌听佛经。莫道此生沉黑海，性中自有大光明。——打一物。
hints: 佛堂里供着，昼夜不灭。
一大碗油，一根灯芯，点在佛前。

zh.q: 萤。——打一字。
hints: 古人说，萤火虫是腐草化成的。
「草」字头，底下一个「化」。

zh.q: 溪壑分离，红尘游戏，真何趣？名利犹虚，后事终难继。——打一俗物。
hints: 众人猜过和尚、道士、偶戏人，都不是。
离了山林，在街上翻跟头给人看；末一句——它的尾巴是剁了的。

zh.at: 魏武题门作「活」字，杨修解
zh.q: 新修的相国府门上，题一个「活」字。——打一字。
hints: 曹操题在门上，杨修看了，叫人把门拆了重修。
嫌门太大了——门里一个「活」。

zh.q: 黄绢幼妇，外孙齑臼。——打四个字。
hints: 拆着读：黄绢是有颜色的丝，幼妇是少女……
色丝合成「绝」；照这个法子，少女、女子、受辛各是一个字。

zh.q: 一杯酪，盖上题个「合」字，传给众人。——打一句话。
hints: 把「合」字拆开看。
上头「人」，中间「一」，底下「口」。

zh.q: 一月复一月，两月共半边，上有可耕之田，下有长流之川；六口共一室，两口不团圆。——打一字。
hints: 两个「月」各借半边，并在一处。
「田」在上，「川」在下，数一数里头的「口」。

zh.q: 画时圆，写时方，寒时短，热时长。——打一字。
hints: 画它是一个圈，写它是一个方框。
冬天它待得短，夏天待得长。

zh.q: 东海有一鱼，无头亦无尾，除去脊梁骨，便是这个字。——打一字。
hints: 从「鱼」字下手。
去了头、去了尾，剩一个「田」；再抽掉中间一竖。

zh.q: 方圆大小随人，腹里文章儒雅。有时满面红妆，常在风前月下。——打一物。
hints: 账上落款，最后要按它一下。
蘸了印泥，一脸通红。

zh.q: 我有一张琴，丝弦长在腹。时时马上弹，弹尽天下曲。——打一物。
hints: 木匠的家什，「马」是他架木头的木马。
线缠在肚里，拉出来一弹，木头上一道直直的黑线。

zh.q: 都来一尺长，上面都是节。两头非常冷，中间非常热。——打一物。
hints: 一年一本，过一天翻一页。
上面的「节」是节气；两头是冬，中间是夏。

zh.q: 大者两支，小者三支，十枚共计二十八支。——打一物。
hints: 长在你身上，一共十个。
大拇指两节，别的都是三节。

zh.q: 八尺一片，四角两面，所识是人面，不识畜生面。——打一物。
hints: 每天早上都要用它。
只擦人的脸，不擦牲口的脸。

zh.at: 《冷斋夜话》，王安石笑曰「此特棋隐语也」
zh.q: 彼亦不敢先，此亦不敢先，惟其不敢先，是以无所争，惟其无所争，故能入于不死不生。——打一物。
hints: 两个人对坐，谁也不肯先动。
一盘下成了不死不生——黑白双活。

zh.q: 可以托六尺之孤，可以寄百里之命。遇刚则铿尔有声，遇柔则没齿无怨。——打一物。
hints: 穿在脚上，一个人全身都托给它。
踩在石板上咯噔响，踩进泥里，「齿」就没了进去。

zh.q: 用之则行，舍之则藏，惟我与尔。危而不持，颠而不扶，将焉用彼。——打一物。
hints: 老人家出门才带上它。
人走不稳了靠它扶——它不扶，要它何用？

zh.q: 倚阑干东君去也，眺花间红日西沉，闪多娇情人不见，闷淹淹笑语无心。——打一字。
hints: 每一句头一个字，都有同一个字框。
阑去了「柬」，间去了「日」，闪去了「人」，闷去了「心」。

zh.q: 上不在上，下不在下，不可在上，止宜在下。——打一字。
hints: 在「上」「下」「不」「止」四个字里，找它们都有的那一笔。
一笔就写完。

zh.q: 二形一体，四支八头。四八一八，飞泉仰流。——打一字。
hints: 这是最早有名的字谜，南朝鲍照作的。
两横两竖；打水往上提，泉水是倒着流的。

zh.q: 若教有口便哑，且要无心为恶。中间全没肚肠，外面强生棱角。——打一字。
hints: 作谜的人姓陈，这个字就是他的名。
添个「口」是「哑」，添个「心」是「恶」。

zh.at: 《魏书·咸阳王禧传》，尹龙虎谓之是箸（禧解作眼）
zh.q: 眠则俱眠，起则俱起，贪如豺狼，赃不入己。——打一物。
hints: 一对儿，总是一起躺下、一起起来。
饭菜都经它夹，一口也落不到它自己肚里。

zh.q: 言与司合，安上已脱，芝芙草拔。——打四个字。
hints: 「言」与「司」合成一个字；「安」去了上头；「芝」「芙」拔了草。
这是赵明诚梦里的话，后来他娶了李清照。

zh.q: 左七右七，横山倒出。——打一字。
hints: 左边是「女」。
「山」横过来倒着写，是「彐」。

zh.q: 一轮月傍窗纱。光明其实堪夸。忽然遇着你和咱。咱觑你，你疑咱。好共歹，莫嗟呀。——打一物。
hints: 圆圆一面，亮得像月亮。
你看它，它也看你——里头那个就是你自己。

zh.q: 长桥两座谁能砌。彩色真奇异。明主赋新诗。日出天初霁。为多情，惊散了。襄王云雨。——打一物。
hints: 雨刚停，太阳一出来才有。
天上一座彩色的桥。

zh.q: 堪笑对头两个。终朝卖弄家私。磨来去去堪参差。总为货财交易。只管掂近播两。那知上下高低。营盘人马两边齐。打个遂心如意。——打一物。
hints: 两头各一个盘子，面对面。
称银子用的，两边一样重才平。

zh.q: 一物生来尖巧。皮肤黑似乌油。朝朝流荡碧滩头。夜静方才罢手。此日难容梗直。全凭委曲相求。昔贤以此傲王侯。传得高名甚久。——打一物。
hints: 天天在水边，直的可不行。
姜太公靠它钓来了周文王——不过他那一枚是直的。

zh.q: 混沌初分出世。阴阳二气生成。元元不损本来真。暂尔藏头缩颈。悟破其中关窍。方才跳出红尘。金蝉脱壳好翻身。早把迷人唤醒。——打一物。
hints: 里头一黄一白，像阴阳还没分开。
壳一破，钻出来的那只，天亮了叫人起床。

zh.q: 火嘴儿窝业的好。只是喉咙小。一条黑肚肠。闷气知多少。——打一物。
hints: 嘴上点着火。
老汉吧嗒吧嗒，吸的是它。

zh.q: 自幼深知水性。江湖游览逍遥。黄家坝与段家桥。却也有时走到。明月常为伴侣。身边落落无交。风流摆摆又摇摇。赚了许多钱钞。——打一物。
hints: 一辈子在水上。
摇摇摆摆载人过河，收几文渡钱。

zh.q: 好日子，也曾过。到如今，没奈何。两片皮任你来点污。清白莫要讲。身子在水里拖。尝尽了苦辣酸甜。哥，揉搓杀了我。——打一物。
hints: 厨房里、桌子上，哪里脏就到哪里。
原是一块好布，如今天天在水里搓。

zh.q: 曾伴你，曾伴你，花前月下。曾伴你，曾伴你，绣阁窗纱。曾伴你，曾伴你，清宵余话。奴本心儿细。你把我当作个寡油花。逞起了风狂。哥，消磨也无半霎。——打一物。
hints: 夜里点着，陪人说话。
心儿细细一根，风一狂就灭了。

zh.q: 一道黄墙。两条湾路。眼放金光。不知其数。——打一物。
hints: 做针线活时戴在指头上。
铜的一圈，满身小坑，顶着针尾往里推。

zh.q: 囫囵一家当。俏身躯，此内藏。心思万种怎安放。东风过墙。空怀怨伤。一朝了却生前帐。俊娇娘。莹莹玉体。载取上吴航。——打一物。
hints: 里头那个，是吐丝把自己裹起来的。
缫出丝来，好织绸缎。

zh.q: 体势甚圆全。木装成，铁裹边。周身内外多光旋。齐头并肩。从无怨言。公平到处人争羡。好寻钱。堆金积玉。买卖已多年。——打一物。
hints: 米店里量米用的。
装满了，拿一根木条一刮——正好一斗。

en.q: Hick-a-more, Hack-a-more, / On the king's kitchen-door; / All the king's horses, / And all the king's men, / Couldn't drive Hick-a-more, Hack-a-more, / Off the king's kitchen-door!
hints: It comes in at the kitchen door every fine morning.
No horse can push it out; only a cloud can take it away.

en.q: When I was taken from the fair body, / They then cut off my head, / And thus my shape was altered; / It's I that make peace between king and king, / And many a true lover glad: / All this I do and ten times more, / And more I could do still, / But nothing can I do, / Without my guider's will.
hints: It was once a feather on a bird.
Treaties and love letters alike are written with it.

en.q: As I was going o'er London Bridge, / I met a cart full of fingers and thumbs!
hints: Fingers and thumbs, but no hands inside them.
You wear a pair of them in winter.

en.q: As soft as silk, as white as milk, / As bitter as gall, a thick wall, / And a green coat covers me all.
hints: It grows on a tree and falls in autumn.
A green husk, a hard shell, a bitter skin, and white meat inside.

en.q: As I was going o'er Tipple Tine, / I met a flock of bonny swine; / Some green-lapp'd, / Some green-back'd; / They were the very bonniest swine / That e'er went over Tipple Tine.
hints: They aren't swine at all: they fly, and they hum.
They live in a hive and make honey.

en.q: In marble walls as white as milk, / Lined with a skin as soft as silk; / Within a fountain crystal clear, / A golden apple doth appear. / No doors there are to this strong-hold. / Yet things break in and steal the gold.
hints: A hen leaves it in the straw.
Crack the white wall: the golden apple is the yolk.

en.q: Arthur O'Bower has broken his band, / He comes roaring up the land;-- / The King of Scots, with all his power, / Cannot turn Arthur of the Bower!
hints: You can hear him roaring, but you never see him.
He breaks branches and lifts roofs; no king can turn him back.

en.q: Flour of England, fruit of Spain, / Met together in a shower of rain; / Put in a bag tied round with a string, / If you'll tell me this riddle, I'll give you a ring.
hints: You eat it at Christmas.
Flour and raisins, boiled in a cloth bag.

en.q: Higher than a house, higher than a tree; / Oh, whatever can that be?
hints: You only see it at night.
It twinkles.

en.q: Old mother Twitchett had but one eye, / And a long tail which she let fly; / And every time she went over a gap, / She left a bit of her tail in a trap.
hints: She lives in the sewing basket.
Her one eye is where the thread goes in.

en.q: Little Nancy Etticoat, / In a white petticoat, / And a red nose; / The longer she stands, / The shorter she grows.
hints: You light her at night.
The red nose is her flame; she melts as she burns.

en.q: Long legs, crooked thighs, / Little head and no eyes.
hints: They live by the fireplace.
Two long iron legs that pinch up the coals.

en.q: Thirty white horses upon a red hill, / Now they tramp, now they champ, now they stand still.
hints: Every one of you has them, in your mouth.
The red hill is your gums.

en.q: Black we are, but much admired; / Men seek for us till they are tired. / We tire the horse, but comfort man / Tell me this riddle if you can.
hints: Miners dig for it deep underground.
Horses haul it in heavy carts; it keeps the hearth warm.

en.q: Purple, yellow, red, and green, / The king cannot reach it nor the queen; / Nor can old Noll, whose power's so great: / Tell me this riddle while I count eight.
hints: You see it after rain.
Colours bent across the sky in a bow.

en.q: Black within, and red without; / Four corners round about.
hints: It stands on the roof.
Soot inside, red bricks outside, and smoke coming out of the top.

en.q: As I went over Lincoln bridge / I met mister Rusticap; / Pins and needles on his back, / A going to Thorney fair.
hints: A small animal that rolls into a ball.
The pins and needles are his spines.

en.q: Formed long ago, yet made to-day, / Employed while others sleep; / What few would like to give away, / Nor any wish to keep.
hints: You make it every morning.
You lie in it at night; nobody wants to give up theirs, and nobody wants to keep to it when ill.

en.q: A riddle, a riddle, as I suppose, / A hundred eyes, and never a nose.
hints: It's used to sift the ashes in the kitchen.
All holes and a rim: the eyes are the holes.

en.q: As round as an apple, as deep as a cup, / And all the king's horses can't pull it up.
hints: You draw water from it.
A round hole dug in the ground, lined with stones.

en.q: As I went through the garden gap, / Who should I meet but Dick Red-cap! / A stick in his hand, a stone in his throat, / If you'll tell me this riddle, I'll give you a groat.
hints: A small red fruit.
The stick is its stalk, the stone its pit.

en.q: Highty, tighty, paradighty clothed in green, / The king could not read it, no more could the queen; / They sent for a wise man out of the East, / Who said it had horns, but was not a beast!
hints: It stays green all winter.
Its prickly leaves are the horns; it bears red berries at Christmas.

en.q: Lives in winter, / Dies in summer, / And grows with its root upwards!
hints: It hangs from the roof in winter.
It drips away and is gone in the sun.

en.q: What shoe-maker makes shoes without leather, / With all the four elements put together? / Fire and water, earth and air; / Ev'ry customer has two pair.
hints: His customers have four feet.
He works with fire and an anvil, nailing iron to hooves.

en.q: I went to the wood and got it, / I sat me down and looked at it; / The more I looked at it the less I liked it, / And I brought it home because I couldn't help it.
hints: He never meant to get it in the wood.
It's stuck in his foot: the more he looks, the less he likes it.

en.q: What is that which has one voice and yet becomes four-footed and two-footed and three-footed?
hints: The Sphinx asked it at Thebes; Oedipus answered.
A baby crawls, a grown-up walks, an old man leans on a stick.

en.q: Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.
hints: Samson set it at his wedding feast; he had killed a lion on the road.
When he passed the lion's carcass again, bees had made something sweet inside it.
